A Sufi teacher who founded the Mouride brotherhood in 1883 and the holy city of Touba in 1887, and whose teachings shape Senegalese Islam today.

He taught that work is a form of prayer and that disciples should give total loyalty to their sheikh. Fearing his growing following after the fall of the Wolof kings such as Lat Dior, the French exiled him to Gabon from 1895 to 1902 and then to Mauritania. He answered with prayer, not war, and his fame grew. His disciples became the main groundnut growers and later traders across the world. Each year millions travel to Touba for the Grand Magal, which marks his departure into exile. See also the Great Mosque of Touba and Sufism.
